subject: Azure private plan - billing cadence & SLA credit mechanics
messages:
From: Caleb Wright <caleb.wright@aureliahealth.com>

Subject: Azure private plan - billing cadence & SLA credit mechanics

Hi Jonas / Redwood team,

Thanks for the demo last week — the private plan flow looks promising for our regulated workloads. Before we move to PO, legal/procurement asked for two things we need clarified so we can finalize internal approvals: 

1) Billing cadence: Aurelia prefers quarterly invoices (one invoice per quarter) to align with our procurement cycle. Can Redwood support quarterly invoicing for a Private Azure offer, or is monthly billing required because of marketplace settlement rules? If quarterly is possible, we need to understand proration rules when the committed usage tier changes mid-quarter.

2) SLA credits and calculation window: We need a clear example of how token-level SLA credits are computed. Specifically: what is the lookback window for missed latency SLOs (per-minute, hourly, monthly), and how are credits capped per invoice or per quarter? A simple worked example would help our finance team.

Attached is our standard PO template (Aurelia_PO_template.docx) — please review and confirm any fields you cannot accept. Also share a sample invoice or usage statement format so our AP team can validate the fields they need.

Appreciate a quick response — this is the last item blocking sign-off on our end.

Regards,
Caleb Wright
Senior Procurement Manager
Aurelia Therapeutics
procurement@aureliahealth.com

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Azure private plan - billing cadence & SLA credit mechanics

Caleb — thanks for the clear ask and for the template. Short answers up front: we can accommodate quarterly billing for Azure Private offers with a monthly reconciliation statement, and SLA credits are calculated monthly and applied on the next invoice (so they can be presented on the quarterly invoice as aggregated credits).

A bit more detail:
- Billing cadence: Redwood issues seller invoices; Azure Marketplace settlement is independent. For private plans we support a quarterly invoicing cadence, but we require monthly usage extracts so we can reconcile chargebacks. If you move between committed tiers mid-quarter we prorate the committed portion at the month boundary (i.e., proration happens at the calendar month).
- SLA credits: Our standard is to evaluate latency/availability per calendar month. If the SLO is missed for a given month, we apply a credit equal to X% of that month's bill for the affected sku (formula: credit = min(monthly_charge * breach_factor, monthly_charge * credit_cap)). Credits aggregate and appear on the next invoice. We can cap credits per quarter — happy to agree a 10% quarterly cap if that helps procurement.

I'm attaching a sample invoice and a short worked example so finance can see the math. Ben — can you confirm technical confirmation on proration windows and whether we need a special clause in the PO for marketplace settlement timing? Marissa — legal redlines on the PO DPA will be needed (Caleb attached Aurelia's PO template).

Propose a short call Wednesday to walk through the sample invoice and the proration example.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Head of Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
jonas@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

Subject: Re: Azure private plan - billing cadence & SLA credit mechanics

Folks — quick operational notes from billing/ops: 

1) Marketplace vs seller invoice: For Azure Private Offers we (the seller) can generate an invoice to Aurelia. Azure will still record a marketplace settlement, but Aurelia's AP team can rely on the seller invoice for payment. We'll include a marketplace reference field for your ledger.

2) Proration and committed tiers: We prorate at the first of the month. If Aurelia ups/downs a committed tier mid-month, usage above/below the new tier is handled in the following month's reconciliation. That keeps the math simple and matches our monitoring windows.

3) SLA credit example (attached diagram): We evaluate SLO breaches on a monthly basis; if a monthly breach occurs we compute the proportional credit for that month and apply it to the next invoice. If you choose quarterly invoices, credits from each month in the quarter are summed and shown on the quarter invoice. We can set a quarterly cap — 10% is reasonable and prevents runaway exposure.

4) AP fields: please confirm you need (a) marketplace reference, (b) Redwood tax id, (c) remit-to address, (d) PO number on invoice. We can include all.

Marissa — billing flow diagram attached; legal will need to confirm whether the PO template requires a separate DPA amendment or if appendable terms suffice.

Ben Carter
Director, Revenue Operations
ben_carter@redwood.com

Jonas / team — thanks for the quick turnaround and the attachments. Aurelia is comfortable moving forward under the following terms: 

- Quarterly seller invoices are acceptable, provided Redwood supplies monthly usage statements (line-item token counts, sku breakdown, and marketplace reference) within five business days of month close.
- Quarterly invoice should include aggregated SLA credits computed monthly and capped at 10% per quarter.
- Payment terms: Net 30 from invoice receipt.
- PO: we'll proceed with our PO template provided earlier; if Redwood needs a DPA amendment please send redlines (we can accept a one-off addendum attached to the PO).

If this captures it, please send a DocuSign with (1) the PO acceptance and (2) a short SOW referencing the Azure private plan sku and committed tiers for Q3. Also include a sample monthly usage statement format so our AP team can map fields.

Let's aim to have the DocuSign out by EOD Monday and a kickoff call the following Tuesday.

Regards,
Caleb Wright
